answer: The tundra of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a verbs first, step by step register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, converted to a slow vesting stream, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Work waits on the plume until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the meadow of the next round.
